text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- National Electirc Power Authority gets green light to disconnect government establishments if they don't pay their electricity bills.
- Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation seeks upward review of the allocation from proceeds of domestic petrol sales, says it needs 5.00 naira per litre instead of its current 1.70 naira per litre.
- External auditors of Savannah Bank raise serious doubts about its ability to continue, because of deficiency in share capital and reserves.
- Government will this month establish mobile magistrates courts at seaports to summarily try people without authorisation to be there.
- Stock exchange revokes licences of 21 stockbroking companies for failing to pay yearly registration charges and protection funds for investors.
- Banks lobby for money from Petroleum Trust Fund.
- Britain is unhappy with the outcome of a mission by Commonwealth officials last week, which paved the way for a ministerial level visit to Nigeria.
